documents.title: Optional Guidelines for AI Use in Courses
documents.summary: Provost-hosted optional guidelines giving instructors four permission levels from open use to strict prohibition, sample syllabus text for each, a menu of allowable use types with allowed and not-allowed examples, a list of unacceptable uses and a disclosure template. Explicitly guidelines only and not official policy.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Faculty may select from among four different permission levels' and calls itself 'guidelines only', so it sets no university-wide stance and offers tiers (Open Use, Moderate Use, Moderate Prohibition, Strict Prohibition); per the codebook, stance is delegates with tiers listed.

units.why: States the guidelines' status: 'guidelines only and do not constitute official university policy'. This sets the scope and force of an institution-level framework, so P56 (framework/scope) and not a stance type; modality informs.
units.anchor: The recommendations here are guidelines only and do not constitute official university policy.

units.why: The purpose line says the guidelines give 'a shared vocabulary for when/how AI may be used in any course context', a statement of purpose and scope of the framework, so P56 rather than P05 (it does not itself define the levels).
units.anchor: a shared vocabulary for when/how AI may be used in any course context
units.policy: The guidelines give instructors and students a shared vocabulary for when/how AI may be used in any course context.

units.why: The guidelines 'complement' the Academic Integrity Policy and department or college policies, which states how this framework sits within other rules; scope and framework, P56.
units.anchor: complements the Academic Integrity Policy
units.policy: The guidelines complement the Academic Integrity Policy and any department- or college-specific policies.

units.why: 'Instructors are invited to select and integrate the items that make the most sense for them' leaves the choice to each instructor, so P04 (instructor sets the rule) with modality may.
units.anchor: Instructors are invited to select and integrate the items that make the most sense
units.policy: Instructors are invited to select and integrate the items that make the most sense for them, given their course and curricular contexts.

units.why: 'Faculty should consider taking Teaching with AI at Auburn' recommends faculty development before setting policy; P63 (support faculty in learning AI).
units.anchor: should consider taking Teaching with AI at Auburn

units.why: 'Students should consider taking A Guide to AI Enhanced Learning' recommends a course on using AI; closest is P44 (courses teach AI use as a skill), not P12 since it is a learning resource rather than a permitted use.
units.anchor: Students should consider taking A Guide to AI Enhanced Learning

units.why: 'Faculty may share these principles with students as a point of discussion about AI ethics' is about communicating expectations to students; no type is specifically about discussing principles, so P56 (framework principles) is the best fit.
units.anchor: Faculty may share these principles with students as a point of discussion
units.policy: Faculty may share these principles with students as a point of discussion about AI ethics and acceptable practices.

units.why: 'You are responsible for the work you submit and for meeting learning goals' makes students answerable for submissions: P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the work you submit and for meeting learning goals.

units.why: 'You should be explicit about whether, how, and why AI was used' asks students to disclose AI use: P24 (disclose), modality should.
units.anchor: You should be explicit about whether, how, and why AI was used

units.why: 'You should document prompts, decisions, and verification steps' asks students to keep records of their AI use, scaled to the assignment; P26 (keep logs/reflections) fits better than P24 because it concerns documentation beyond a disclosure note.
units.anchor: You should document prompts, decisions, and verification steps proportionate to the assignment

units.why: For faculty: 'Acknowledging your use of AI tools for creating course materials' is a faculty-facing principle about AI-made materials: P48.
units.anchor: Acknowledging your use of AI tools for creating course materials
units.policy: Faculty should consider acknowledging their use of AI tools for creating course materials.

units.why: 'Disclosing your use of AI tools' under faculty principles asks instructors to disclose their own AI use: P47.
units.anchor: Disclosing your use of AI tools
units.policy: Faculty should consider disclosing their use of AI tools.

units.why: 'Avoiding submitting personally identifiable or FERPA-protected student information to AI tools that have not been vetted' is a privacy rule for faculty; P50 (protect personal data, vetted tools).
units.anchor: Avoiding submitting personally identifiable or FERPA-protected student information to AI tools
units.policy: Faculty should consider avoiding submitting personally identifiable or FERPA-protected student information to AI tools that have not been vetted and approved by the university, including for automated assessment.

units.why: 'Reducing or eliminating the use of AI detectors, which are unreliable and easily fooled' advises against relying on detectors: P39.
units.anchor: Reducing or eliminating the use of AI detectors, which are unreliable and easily fooled
units.policy: Faculty should consider reducing or eliminating the use of AI detectors, which are unreliable and easily fooled.

units.why: 'Faculty may select from among four different permission levels' sets up named tiers, so P05 rather than P04 (it names the levels, not just who decides).
units.anchor: Faculty may select from among four different permission levels for their assignments, courses, or curricula.

units.why: Option 1 'AI is encouraged across the workflow (brainstorm to draft to revise)' defines the open tier as encouraging AI: P02.
units.anchor: AI is encouraged across the workflow (brainstorm → draft → revise) while meeting learning goals

units.why: The same Option 1 sentence adds 'students must disclose use and verification'; a separate disclosure rule, P24, must.
units.anchor: students must disclose use and verification

units.why: Option 2 'AI use is allowed for most stages' defines the moderate tier as default-permitting with conditions: P02, modality may.
units.anchor: AI use is allowed for most stages

units.why: Option 2 requires 'an AI disclosure note describing how they used it and how they verified results', a per-submission disclosure: P24.
units.anchor: students must include an AI disclosure note describing how they used it
units.policy: Students must include an AI disclosure note describing how they used AI and how they verified results.

units.why: Option 3 permits AI only 'for tasks not directly related to the creation of a final product (e.g., debug hints, study tool)'. P12 (study/tutor use) chosen because the permitted range is general study and hints; P13 covers only debugging, so does not fit as well.
units.anchor: tasks not directly related to the creation of a final product
units.policy: AI may be used for tasks not directly related to the creation of a final product (e.g., debug hints, study tool).

units.why: Option 4 'AI use is not permitted' is a blanket ban: P01.
units.anchor: AI use is not permitted.

units.why: 'students are encouraged to use Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot' in the Option 1 syllabus text encourages AI use by default in that course: P02.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to use Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot

units.why: The Option 1 text says 'students must disclose any AI-generated material they use and properly attribute it, including in-text citations': P24.
units.anchor: students must disclose any AI-generated material they use and properly attribute it

units.why: 'avoid sharing any sensitive or private information' with public AI tools (PII, PHI, financial data, IP) is a data-protection rule: P50.
units.anchor: avoid sharing any sensitive or private information

units.why: 'Microsoft Copilot is available by logging in with their AU email and password' names a university-provided tool with enterprise data protection: P17.
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot is available by logging in with their AU email and password
units.policy: Microsoft Copilot, a private AI tool with Enterprise Level Data Protection, is available by logging in with an AU email and password.

units.why: The statement 'acknowledge the use of [Generative AI Tool Name and version]... was used in the following way(s)' prescribes a disclosure naming tool, version and how it was used: P25 (tool details) over P24 since the template's point is the specific details.
units.anchor: acknowledge the use of [Generative AI Tool Name and version], a language model developed by
units.policy: A student includes in assignments a statement acknowledging the use of the Generative AI Tool, with its name, version and provider, and the way(s) it was used.

units.why: Option 2 syllabus text permits AI 'for specific assignments or activities, as designated by the instructor': the instructor decides per assignment, P04.
units.anchor: for specific assignments or activities, as designated by the instructor

units.why: Option 3 text 'all submitted work is produced by the students themselves' states the own-work requirement: P29.
units.anchor: all submitted work is produced by the students themselves

units.why: 'Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot for graded assignments' bans AI on graded work: P01.
units.anchor: Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot for graded assignments
units.policy: Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot for graded assignments.

units.why: 'Use of a Generative AI Tool to complete an assignment constitutes academic dishonesty' classifies misuse as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: Use of a Generative AI Tool to complete an assignment constitutes academic dishonesty.

units.why: 'Students may use Generative AI tools as a study tool' under Option 3 allows study use: P12.
units.anchor: Students may use Generative AI tools as a study tool

units.why: 'AI tools are not trustworthy' warns that output may be wrong, so P31 (verify output).
units.anchor: be forewarned that AI tools are not trustworthy

units.why: Option 4 text 'Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot' with no graded-work limiter bans all AI use in the course: P01.
units.anchor: Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like ChatGPT or Copilot.

units.why: Faculty who allow AI 'should select one or more of the following descriptions of use types, copy the text into the syllabus or assignment': a menu of named use categories, P05.
units.anchor: they should select one or more of the following descriptions of use types

units.why: The content-tutor use type 'Clarify concepts, suggest readings, pose practice questions, help brainstorm' allows AI as a tutor: P12.
units.anchor: Clarify concepts, suggest readings, pose practice questions, help brainstorm, or ask questions for understanding.

units.why: For coding/homework, 'explain error messages; suggest debugging strategies (no final solutions unless allowed)' allows debugging help: P13.
units.anchor: explain error messages; suggest debugging strategies (no final solutions unless allowed).

units.why: 'create practice questions; simulate step-by-step walkthroughs of techniques' allows study aids: P14.
units.anchor: create practice questions; simulate step-by-step walkthroughs of techniques

units.why: 'Completing graded products for you (e.g., paper, code, slide deck)' is listed as not allowed: AI may not produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: Completing graded products for you (e.g., paper, code, slide deck)
units.policy: AI may not be used for completing graded products for you (e.g., paper, code, slide deck).

units.why: 'Generating or altering data' is listed as not allowed for the tutor use type. It is AI producing submitted material, so P19 is the closest type.
units.anchor: Generating or altering data
units.policy: AI may not be used for generating or altering data.

units.why: 'Answering graded quiz/test items' is not allowed: no AI on tests, P22.
units.anchor: Answering graded quiz/test items
units.policy: AI may not be used for answering graded quiz/test items.

units.why: The writing-feedback use type allows AI to 'Review completed drafts for grammar/clarity/tone after you write your own text': prose-specific rule, P18.
units.anchor: Review completed drafts for grammar/clarity/tone after you write your own text.

units.why: 'Summarizing or paraphrasing others' work' is not allowed in the writing-feedback use type; a prose rule, P18.
units.anchor: Summarizing or paraphrasing others’ work
units.policy: AI may not be used for summarizing or paraphrasing others' work.

units.why: 'Drafting full papers or sections without your authorship' is not allowed: AI may not produce submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: Drafting full papers or sections without your authorship
units.policy: AI may not be used for drafting full papers or sections without your authorship.

units.why: 'Inventing or citing sources not verified by you' is not allowed; the core point is that students must verify what AI gives them, P31.
units.anchor: Inventing or citing sources not verified by you
units.policy: Inventing or citing sources not verified by you is not allowed.

units.why: The differentiated-support type allows 'Generate study guides or alternative materials from course docs; language support; accessibility aids': P14.
units.anchor: Generate study guides or alternative materials from course docs; language support; accessibility aids

units.why: 'Replacing official accommodations' is not allowed, and the type 'Does not replace accommodations': AI support does not substitute for accommodations, P51.
units.anchor: Replacing official accommodations
units.policy: AI may not be used to replace official accommodations.

units.why: 'Uploading confidential or copyrighted materials not permitted by course policy' is not allowed: P49.
units.anchor: Uploading confidential or copyrighted materials not permitted by course policy
units.policy: Uploading confidential or copyrighted materials not permitted by course policy is not allowed.

units.why: Project-assistant use is 'Allowed only if the assignment permits', an assignment-level permission: P04.
units.anchor: Allowed only if the assignment permits

units.why: 'you must revise in your own voice' makes students own AI-assisted text, P29 (P18 is about prose-specific tools, not ownership).
units.anchor: you must revise in your own voice

units.why: 'Submitting AI-written sections as your own without permission and revision' is not allowed: AI may not produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-written sections as your own without permission and revision
units.policy: Submitting AI-written sections as your own without permission and revision is not allowed.

units.why: 'Bypassing personal reflection or show-your-work components' is not allowed: AI must not replace the student's own thinking, P32.
units.anchor: Bypassing personal reflection or ‘show-your-work’ components
units.policy: Bypassing personal reflection or 'show-your-work' components is not allowed.

units.why: Technical-colleague use is 'Use only if explicitly allowed': AI use is barred unless the assignment says so, a fallback rule, P06.
units.anchor: Use only if explicitly allowed

units.why: 'you can explain results line-by-line' requires students to be able to explain AI-assisted technical work: P30.
units.anchor: you can explain results line-by-line

units.why: For coding/homework, 'debug suggestions; unit-test scaffolds; refactoring ideas you understand' lists permitted technical help. P13 chosen because debugging comes first; P16 does not fit since no generated code submission is stated.
units.anchor: debug suggestions; unit-test scaffolds; refactoring ideas you understand.

units.why: 'code comments; plotting templates you adapt to your own data' allows AI-generated code with a condition (adapt to own data): P16.
units.anchor: code comments; plotting templates you adapt to your own data.

units.why: 'Submitting code you can't explain' is not allowed: students must understand submitted code, P30.
units.anchor: Submitting code you can’t explain
units.policy: Submitting code you can't explain is not allowed.

units.why: 'Using generated code to complete graded tasks when not allowed' bars AI-produced code on graded work absent permission: P19.
units.anchor: Using generated code to complete graded tasks when not allowed
units.policy: Using generated code to complete graded tasks when not allowed is not allowed.

units.why: Unacceptable uses 'should be communicated with students proactively, rather than assumed' tells instructors to state expectations: P09 (state it in the syllabus/assignment) chosen as nearest.
units.anchor: should be communicated with students proactively, rather than assumed

units.why: 'Submitting AI-generated work as your own learning/performance when the assignment requires your original analysis, code, design, or voice' is unacceptable: P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated work as your own learning/performance

units.why: 'Fabrication/falsification: invented sources, data, citations, images, or results' is deemed unacceptable. It is a ban on fabricating content, which no type covers (P19 is about generating submitted work; P31 is about verifying output).
units.anchor: Fabrication/falsification: invented sources, data, citations, images, or results.
units.policy: Fabrication or falsification (invented sources, data, citations, images, or results) is unacceptable.
units.uncovered_note: Ban on fabricating or falsifying sources, data, citations, images or results with AI.

units.why: 'Undisclosed use: using AI even where allowed but not disclosing how' makes nondisclosure itself unacceptable: P28.
units.anchor: Undisclosed use: using AI even where allowed but not disclosing how.

units.why: 'Bypassing learning goals' such as using AI for show-your-work, reflection or lab notebook steps 'that assess your own reasoning' keeps the student as thinker: P32.
units.anchor: Bypassing learning goals: e.g., using AI to complete

units.why: 'uploading confidential/regulated data (FERPA/PII/PHI) or proprietary content to consumer tools' is a privacy and legal violation: P50.
units.anchor: uploading confidential/regulated data (FERPA/PII/PHI) or proprietary content to consumer tools

units.why: The heading 'Required Disclosure: AI Contributions (add to end of submissions)' requires an AI disclosure with every submission: P24.
units.anchor: Required Disclosure: AI Contributions (add to end of submissions)

units.why: The APA example 'ChatGPT (Sept. 29 version) [Large language model]' shows how to cite the tool, version and date: P25.
units.anchor: OpenAI. (2025). ChatGPT (Sept. 29 version) [Large language model].
units.policy: An AI tool is cited in APA 7 form with provider, year, tool name and version, and a note that it is a large language model.

units.why: The MLA example includes 'Prompt: Explain CRISPR base editing for a lay audience.', so the citation records the exact prompt and date: P25.
units.anchor: Prompt: “Explain CRISPR base editing for a lay audience.” Response to [Your Name].
units.policy: An AI tool is cited in MLA 9 form with the tool, provider, date, and the exact prompt.

units.why: The instructor paste-in says 'All other uses are prohibited' beyond tasks the instructor lists, a per-assignment allowlist with prohibited fallback: P06.
units.anchor: for these tasks only: [list tasks from the menu]. All other uses are prohibited.

units.why: 'You must credit your use in an AI Contributions note' requires disclosure with the submission: P24.
units.anchor: You must credit your use in an ‘AI Contributions’ note.

documents.unit: Biggio Center for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning
documents.title: Syllabus Language for Generative Artificial Intelligence
tiers: Option 3B Strict Use (no AI for assignments, study tool ok)
documents.summary: Teaching-center page offering four ready-to-paste syllabus statements, from open use with attribution to a full ban, plus a note that AI tools must be vetted. Instructors pick the one matching their desired level.
documents.stance_why: The page says it 'suggests one of four syllabus statements depending on the instructor's desired level of use', so it sets no single stance and hands the choice to instructors with tiers; stance is delegates.

units.why: 'suggests one of four syllabus statements depending on the instructor's desired level of use' offers tiered statements for instructors to choose: P05.
units.anchor: suggests one of four syllabus statements depending on the instructor's desired level of use

units.why: 'All technology must be vetted through the Auburn University vetting process prior to use' requires vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: All technology must be vetted through the Auburn University vetting process prior to use.

units.anchor: Embrace and encourage AI use in assignments, with the requirement that students

units.why: Option 1 text: 'students must disclose any AI-generated material they use and properly attribute it': P24.
units.anchor: students must disclose any AI-generated material they use and properly attribute it

units.why: 'avoid sharing any sensitive or private information when using these tools' (PII, PHI, financial data, IP) is a data-protection rule: P50.
units.anchor: avoid sharing any sensitive or private information when using these tools

units.why: The template 'acknowledge the use of [Generative AI Tool Name], a language model developed by [Provider]... used in the following way(s)' prescribes a disclosure naming the tool and its use: P25.
units.anchor: acknowledge the use of [Generative AI Tool Name], a language model developed by

units.why: Option 2 'Encourage AI use in specific assignments, but not all' makes AI use assignment by assignment: P04.
units.anchor: Encourage AI use in specific assignments, but not all.

units.why: Option 2 text permits AI 'for specific assignments, as designated by the instructor', so the instructor decides: P04.
units.anchor: for specific assignments, as designated by the instructor

units.why: 'students must disclose any use of AI-generated material' in Option 2 is a disclosure duty: P24.

units.why: Option 3A text 'Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini' bans AI for the course: P01. (The heading calls it 'discourage', but the wording is a ban, so it is not P03.)
units.anchor: Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like Microsoft Copilot
units.policy: Students must not seek the assistance of Generative AI Tools like Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.

units.why: 'all submitted work is produced by the students themselves' states the own-work requirement: P29.
units.anchor: all submitted work is produced by the students themselves

units.anchor: or Gemini for graded assignments.

units.why: 'Students may use Generative AI tools as a study tool' under Option 3B allows study use: P12.
units.anchor: Students may use Generative AI tools as a study tool

units.why: 'AI tools are not trustworthy' warns that output can be wrong: P31.
units.anchor: be forewarned that AI tools are not trustworthy

documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Academic Integrity
documents.title: AI Guidance for Students
documents.summary: Short academic-integrity page for students: check the syllabus and instructor first, submitted work must be your own, verbatim AI output is cheating, and cite AI where allowed in the way the instructor requires.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI stance of its own: it sends students to 'the course syllabus' and instructor for what is authorized and says citation 'may be different from class to class', while banning verbatim AI work; stance is delegates.

units.why: 'review the course syllabus and speak with the instructor to find out what is considered authorized use' tells students to check before using AI: P10.
units.anchor: review the course syllabus and speak with the instructor
units.policy: Before using AI in any assignment, examination, project, etc., students review the course syllabus and speak with the instructor to find out what is considered authorized use of generative AI.

units.why: 'any work turned in must be completely your own work' is the own-work rule: P29.
units.anchor: any work turned in must be completely your own work

units.why: 'Using work produced with AI word for word is considered cheating' classifies verbatim AI output as cheating: P36 (misconduct) rather than P19, because the wording is about how it is classified.
units.anchor: Using work produced with AI word for word is considered cheating.

units.why: 'Strictly using AI to complete your work robs you of the chance to learn the material and hone the skills' gives the learning rationale: P41.
units.anchor: robs you of the chance to learn the material and hone the skills

units.why: 'make sure that you properly attribute this use in the manner expected of you by the instructor' requires attribution where AI is allowed: P24.
units.anchor: properly attribute this use in the manner expected of you by the instructor
units.policy: If certain uses of AI are authorized in the course, students make sure that they properly attribute this use in the manner expected by the instructor.

units.why: 'Your instructor will inform you of the way in which your use of AI should be cited' leaves the citation format to the instructor: P04.
units.anchor: Your instructor will inform you of the way in which your use
units.policy: Your instructor will inform you of the way in which your use of AI should be cited.

units.why: 'the way AI is to be cited may be different from class to class' says rules do not carry across courses: P11.
units.anchor: the way AI is to be cited may be different from class to class

documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Academic Integrity
documents.title: AI Guidance for Faculty
documents.summary: Brief guidance urging faculty to add an AI statement to the syllabus and listing questions to consider, from always allowed to never allowed.
documents.stance_why: The page only says 'It is important to consider adding a statement to a course syllabus' and lists questions for the instructor to decide; it sets no stance, so delegates.

units.why: 'It is important to consider adding a statement to a course syllabus to address the use of AI' asks faculty to put an AI statement in the syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: It is important to consider adding a statement to a course syllabus
units.policy: It is important to consider adding a statement to a course syllabus to address the use of AI.

units.why: 'There are many ways AI can be used including brainstorming ideas, checking grammar, rewriting a student's work, and problem-solving' names kinds of uses that instructors must sort; closest is P05 (categories of use).
units.anchor: brainstorming ideas, checking grammar, rewriting a student’s work, and problem-solving

units.why: 'Consider the following when deciding whether any use of AI will be allowed in the course' leaves the decision to the instructor: P04.
units.anchor: Consider the following when deciding whether any use of AI will be allowed
units.policy: Consider the following when deciding whether any use of AI will be allowed in the course.

units.why: 'you can craft an AI statement for your syllabus that describes what is authorized and unauthorized AI usage' asks instructors to state expectations in the syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: craft an AI statement for your syllabus that describes what is authorized
units.policy: Instructors can craft an AI statement for their syllabus that describes what is authorized and unauthorized AI usage in their class.

documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Academic Integrity
documents.title: Syllabus Support (example academic-integrity statements incl. AI)
documents.summary: Example academic-integrity syllabus statements; two mention AI: one lists unauthorized AI use as a violation and one sample AI statement allows brainstorming and grammar checks but not passing off AI content as original.
documents.stance_why: The page offers example statements for instructors to adapt ('Feel free to use all or parts of these statements') and sets no university AI stance; one sample allows limited AI use, so stance is delegates.

units.why: 'This includes the unauthorized use of AI' in the example violations list classes unauthorized AI use as an academic-integrity violation: P36.
units.anchor: This includes the unauthorized use of AI.

units.why: The AI example says 'students are allowed to use AI to brainstorm ideas': allowed brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: students are allowed to use AI to brainstorm ideas

units.why: The same sentence allows AI to 'check grammar', which is a prose-specific use: P18.
units.anchor: or check grammar

units.why: 'Presenting content generated through AI as original work is considered unauthorized use of AI' bars AI-produced work submitted as one's own: P19.
units.anchor: Presenting content generated through AI as original work is considered unauthorized use of AI.

units.why: 'All students found to have allegedly violated the Academic Integrity Policy will be submitted to the Office of the Provost' sets the reporting route for AI violations: P36.
units.anchor: will be submitted to the Office of the Provost for review and appropriate action

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. Biggio page labels Option 3A 'discourage' but its text is a ban (coded P01). Provost Option 1-2 sample text is repeated on both pages and was coded in each document separately. Academic Integrity Policy PDF not read.
